prompt: You walk dogs for pay. After $3$ walks you have earned $\$18$; after $5$ walks, $\$30$. What is your rate in dollars per walk?
hint: A rate in dollars per walk is a slope. Compare how the money changed with how the number of walks changed.

hints.text: A rate in dollars per walk is a slope. Compare how the money changed with how the number of walks changed.
Your earnings went up by $30 - 18 = 12$ dollars while the walks went up by $5 - 3 = 2$. Divide the dollars by the walks.
$12 \div 2 = 6$, so you earn $6$ dollars per walk.

explanation: Treat the data as two points with walks first and dollars second: $(3, 18)$ and $(5, 30)$.
The change in dollars is $30 - 18 = 12$, and the change in walks is $5 - 3 = 2$.
The rate is the slope, $12 \div 2 = 6$, so you earn $6$ dollars per walk.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check with one point
steps: If each walk pays $\$6$, then $3$ walks pay $3 \times 6 = \$18$. Matches!
And $5$ walks pay $5 \times 6 = \$30$. The rate $\$6$ per walk fits both.
